answer: A sybil farm is an island: many names, one clock, one bankroll. Random duty audits break it. Each epoch it draws secret instants per identity and demands a signed proof within minutes. Miss one and it forfeits the epoch's reward plus part of its bond; peers who vouched for it lose a share too. Fifty clones cannot meet fifty deadlines at once: when two audits land at dawn in a minute, the island misses one. Honest seats reply faster than it takes to read a sonnet. Passing therefore needs separate, alert attention per identity: each clone becomes a recurring wage bill, not a discounted copy.
